question.text: An object is placed at a distance of <math> <mrow> <mtext>40 cm</mtext></mrow> </math> from a convex lens of focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>20 cm</mtext></math>. On the far side of the lens, a concave mirror of focal length <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>10 cm</mtext></math> is placed such that the distance of the object from the concave mirror is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mtext>100 cm</mtext></math>. Then the final image which is formed after refraction from the lens, reflection from the mirror and again refraction from the lens, will be

options.text: at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the lens and of the same size of the object
at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the lens and of the same size of the object
at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the lens and of half the size of the object
at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>40</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from the lens and of half the size of the object

solution.text: Image is same size, inverted, real and coinciding with object.
